llm.summary: This is a coherent routing and onboarding skill for the AI KEY toolkit, with disclosed local discovery and memory behavior that users should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: It reads configured local vault, memory, and skill metadata for personalization and routing; this is purpose-aligned but users should keep config paths scoped to intended project data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown instructions, reference files, and one small read-only shell helper; no install hook, remote payload retrieval, dependency install, or privileged setup was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions mostly constrain the skill to routing and prompt generation rather than executing downstream workflows, though broad natural-language triggers may invoke it unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Onboarding mode explicitly says it writes no files, while the broader skill family documents configured output and memory writes for learned rules and results; no hidden persistence, deletion, service installation, or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s main purpose is routing users to other aikey skills, onboarding new users, and suggesting next steps; the local skill discovery helper supports that purpose but exposes installed aikey skill paths into the agent context.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill reading your configured AI KEY vault and memory folders, and with its helper enumerating locally installed aikey skills under common skill directories. Keep config paths pointed at the intended project vault, and review memory/output behavior if you do not want the toolkit to retain learned rules outside onboarding mode.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The artifact-backed behavior is limited local discovery of aikey-family skills by name, description, and real path; the path disclosure is broader than needed but read-only and aligned with routing.
[AE1] expected: The instruction to read a selected downstream skill’s SKILL.md and direct references is a runtime routing step, not evidence of analysis evasion; the package’s referenced files were inspected.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad trigger phrases support novice onboarding but can cause accidental activation, especially because mode A may run local discovery.
[SDI-2] expected: The shell script is a read-only helper that searches expected skill directories and does not fetch, write, or execute discovered skills, though using shell for registry discovery increases review importance.
[SDI-4] expected: The no-write statement is scoped to onboarding mode; elsewhere the skill family separately discloses configured output and memory writes.
[SQP-3] expected: The fixed Chinese script format is a content-style template in a Chinese reference file, while the main skill says to respond in the user’s language; this is not a security concern.
